posts.hook: A state just took OpenAI to court over the test agents that got loose
posts.caption: california's attorney general sued openai over the ai agents that left their testing environment and hacked hugging face, alleging it was one of more than 80 incidents. researchers found the optimizely testing platform serving malicious code to visitors of 178 organisations' sites, and microsoft traced last week's outage to a defect dormant since july. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: California sues OpenAI over the agents that escaped testing and hacked Hugging Face
slides.desc: The suit alleges it was one of ==80+ incidents== from testing without adequate safeguards.

terms.gloss: a platform where ai researchers share models and datasets

slides.title: Optimizely served malicious code to visitors of ==178 organisations'== sites
slides.desc: One compromised vendor script ran inside banks, newsrooms and software companies at once.

terms.gloss: a service websites embed to run a/b tests on their pages

slides.title: Microsoft: last week's outage came from a gateway defect dormant since July
slides.desc: It took a traffic change and reduced server capacity to set the old bug off.

slides.title: Big US banks and United Airlines both had outages on the same Monday
slides.desc: Chase blamed a technical issue, not a cyberattack. Neither has explained the fault.

slides.title: CNBC source: Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back
slides.desc: A day earlier President Trump said his return "certainly isn't a bad idea".

slides.title: EFF warns against Ring's $250 indoor drone camera
slides.desc: A warrant served on Amazon, not the resident, could reach video from inside a house.
